chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Majestic and Mighty: 'His Chair extends over the heavens and the earth' [2:255] — do the heavens and earth encompass the Chair, or does the Chair encompass the heavens and earth? He said: Rather, the Chair encompasses the heavens and the earth, and the Throne (al-Arsh) and everything — the Chair encompasses all.

key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Throne (Arsh) — the supreme symbol of God's sovereignty, often interpreted as His authority over creation
key_terms.الْكُرْسِيُّ: The Chair/Throne (Kursi) — in Ayat al-Kursi, it symbolizes God's dominion and knowledge; al-Sadiq here clarifies its cosmic vastness
key_terms.وَسِعَ: Encompasses/extends over — the key verb from Ayat al-Kursi, which Zurara's question seeks to clarify

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Kursi and the Arsh in Islamic cosmology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Zurara ibn A'yan, a foremost companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), poses a question about the cosmological scope of the Kursi (Chair/Throne of God) mentioned in Ayat al-Kursi (2:255). Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the Kursi is vaster than the heavens and earth combined, and even encompasses the Arsh (Supreme Throne) and all of creation. This hadith establishes a Shia cosmological hierarchy: Kursi > Arsh > all heavens and earth, indicating that both cosmic structures transcend physical creation and serve as metaphors for God's infinite knowledge and power.
